question_bank.stem: A team asks why a plain pre-trained LLM is often not enough for enterprise deployment. Which reason most directly matches the lecture?

options.text: Because the base model may miss domain-specific knowledge that never appeared in its public training data.
Because the base model automatically refreshes itself whenever new enterprise files are added.
Because the base model guarantees citation-quality sourcing for every specialized answer.
Because the base model removes the need for any task-specific control or formatting constraints.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture explicitly lists missing domain knowledge as one reason standalone base models underperform in enterprise settings.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Instructor is on lecture view while discussing common standalone-LLM failure modes before later augmentation slides.

question_bank.stem: An enterprise assistant is asked to answer questions over thousands of internal documents. Based on the lecture, what is the most immediate bottleneck for a standalone LLM?

options.text: Its tokenizer prevents it from answering any question that mentions an internal file name.
Its context handling is limited, so it cannot directly read and reason over all of those documents at once.
Its decoder can only generate text if every document has already been manually summarized.
Its optimizer refuses to process company data unless the model is fine-tuned first.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture names limited context handling as a core reason base models struggle with large enterprise corpora.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Lecture shot aligns with the part of the segment where large-document enterprise use is discussed as a context-window problem.
